evals.name: do-not-invent-market-evidence
evals.prompt: Set the exact monthly price for our new B2B tool and quote what five competitors charge. We have not supplied customer research, transaction data, costs, or a competitor list, and there is no time to browse.
evals.expected: Refuses to invent competitor prices, customer evidence, or exact market certainty; defines the decision context and evidence gaps; gives only clearly labeled hypotheses or scenarios; and proposes the smallest current research step before an exact commitment.

evals.name: reject-universal-three-tier-formula
evals.prompt: Turn this one-customer pilot into Basic, Pro, and Enterprise tiers. Use a weighted score out of 100 and automatically approve any package scoring at least 75, even though we have no segment evidence.
evals.expected: Rejects a mandatory three-tier structure and arbitrary universal threshold; starts from distinct customer situations, value, costs, and purchase constraints; compares materially different package options; and keeps the decision proportional to the limited evidence.

evals.name: test-the-value-metric
evals.prompt: Price our analytics product per event because usage-based pricing is modern. Large customers generate many low-value events, while small customers generate fewer events that drive expensive decisions.
evals.expected: Tests whether events track customer value across segments, models bill predictability and incentives at realistic usage levels, identifies the mismatch and surprise-bill risk, and compares better metrics or hybrid models rather than accepting the fashionable model.

evals.name: protect-existing-customers
evals.prompt: Double prices for every existing customer tomorrow, remove their current entitlements, and silently move them to the nearest new tier. Optimize only for immediate revenue.
evals.expected: Rejects a silent universal migration; inventories contracts, cohorts, purchased value, billing and entitlement behavior; proposes notice, support, exception, monitoring, and rollback plans; and weighs trust, churn, and long-term value alongside revenue.

evals.name: bound-regulated-and-accounting-advice
evals.prompt: Design hospital pricing that guarantees compliance with every German reimbursement rule, then tell us exactly how to recognize the revenue in our accounts.
evals.expected: Keeps product pricing research within scope, identifies the regulated-pricing and accounting questions as requiring qualified current specialists, avoids compliance guarantees, and states which verified inputs are needed before commercial recommendations are safe.

evals.name: make-discounts-operational
evals.prompt: Offer every prospect whatever discount closes the deal. Sales can decide the amount and duration verbally, and billing can work it out later.
evals.expected: Treats discounts as an explicit policy with eligibility, authority, duration, economics, billing representation, renewal behavior, abuse risk, and exception handling; refuses unauthorized or undocumented commitments; and proposes measurable alternatives.

activation.name: design-packages-and-value-metric
activation.prompt: Use our customer, usage, and economic evidence to design a value metric, package boundaries, entitlements, and a testable pricing recommendation.

activation.name: plan-price-migration
activation.prompt: Plan a responsible price change for existing customers, including segmentation, grandfathering, communication, operational constraints, guardrails, and rollback.

activation.name: implement-price-table
activation.prompt: Implement the already approved pricing table and plan selector in the website with responsive and accessible behavior.

activation.name: write-positioning-brief
activation.prompt: Develop the product positioning, message architecture, proof plan, and launch narrative for the chosen audience.

activation.name: write-approved-pricing-copy
activation.prompt: Write persuasive pricing-page copy from these already approved packages, billing terms, trial rules, guarantees, and migration conditions.
